answer: Every submersible dive is timed from hatch-close to hatch-open, and the log records the depth, the pilot and the purpose of the dive. A marble dive copied from another logbook fails the record: at the mesa of the dive the depth must match the submersible's own instruments, and a copied dive was never made. Faking a dive means launching the submersible, paying the support ship and spending 19,800, and the jetty entry in the dive log is countersigned by the pilot, so a dive with no pilot's signature is struck from the book.
